description: AgroNova is a team passionate about NASA Earth observations, AI, and sustainable agriculture. We aim to build a smart decision-support tool that helps farmers explore crop rotation strategies using satellite data, soil conditions, crop characteristics, and climate information to improve soil health and farm resilience.
summary:
We built TerraShift, a mobile-first Progressive Web App that gives smallholder farmers in Bangladesh’s Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta a climate-adaptive crop rotation plan covering 3 years (12 seasons). A farmer like Rafiq drops a pin on his field. TerraShift then pulls NASA Earth observation data for that location and calculates reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) using the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith method. It feeds the results into a deterministic rule engine validated by agronomists, so every recommendation is transparent and can be repeated.

TerraShift turns satellite-derived climate data into practical decisions for farmers who have no access to soil labs or reliable 4G. The plan helps farmers on about 1.5 hectares cope with erratic monsoons by matching crops to real water demand. It reduces costly groundwater pumping for dry-season Boro rice by suggesting less thirsty alternatives where they make sense. It also brings in legumes and other soil-building crops to restore degraded land.

This matters because millions of delta households depend on rice farming that is becoming riskier as rainfall shifts and aquifers decline. TerraShift puts NASA science in a farmer’s pocket and supports livelihoods, water security and long-term soil health.

Smallholder farmers in the lower Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna delta face erratic monsoons, surging groundwater pumping tariffs for winter Boro rice, and accelerating soil degradation. Most modern digital agriculture solutions require expensive soil laboratory tests or uninterrupted 4G connectivity—luxuries unavailable to 1.5-hectare farmers like Rafiq.
